title: 1926 Mac Service Center end of Maple Street owned by Allan MacIntosh.
description: In November 1921, an association was formed to operate an open skating rink and a baseball diamond in the summer. William Carr was the manager. The surface was 75 x 175 feet. Carnivals, concerts, and various fundraising activities were held in the 1930s to keep the rink in operation. Hockey teams were formed, ice carnivals were added, and even music was included in 1936, with a phonograph and speakers. In 1944, a building was ready for both male and female skaters, the rink walls erected, lights put up, and the ground covered with a layer of sawdust, waiting for freezing weather. The picture shows the rink on the McMullin flat, lower Main Street, with an 80 x 200 feet skating surface, the heated rink house, the ice surface encased in wood walls with the end open for the snow pile after shovelling snow off the ice surface. Various people were hired to manage, and the town's cooperation continued to keep it open. Johnny Sproul was hired in 1955. (Photo courtesy of Don Oliver, early 1950s.)
